feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope of responsibility is consistently impressive. It reads professionally and has good evidence of impact, though it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression align well around digital platform leadership, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Strong credibility: large-scale website migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI search work all signal real ownership of complex initiatives.  
- Writing is polished and mostly error-free, with concise, action-led bullets and relevant technical depth for both strategic and hands-on roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results (conversion, engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost/time savings) would increase impact.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” would read more cleanly as “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value statement plus one scope statement; foreground public-sector digital transformation and enterprise scale.
- Add one concrete signal of scale or complexity already supported elsewhere (for example, enterprise web modernization or multi-publisher environments).
- Replace “behind high-volume public-sector communications” with more direct, outcome-oriented wording.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience driving public-sector digital transformation across enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics and content operations. Leads website modernization, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations with high-volume publishing needs.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of capabilities closely repeats the Core Competencies section; keep the intro broader and more positioning-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership scope will make it feel more distinct and executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim repetitive wording like “communications” and “operations.”
- Prioritize the most senior, differentiating strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel content operations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- If space allows, replace one broad item with a sharper differentiator, e.g., “Drupal-based platform modernization” or “High-volume public-sector publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and recent projects almost verbatim.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps with Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement-focused bullet.
- Tighten wording: e.g., “AI-powered legislative search” instead of “AI-enabled legislative search experience,” and “10'×20'” for style consistency.
- Emphasize distinct value or outcome for each project: discovery, campaign growth, conference engagement, or cross-channel distribution.
- Keep parallel structure across entries, starting each with a strong verb and avoiding long feature lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo experience bullets; keep this section focused on named examples, not responsibilities already described above.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a broad services list. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and Drupal-based campaign delivery for public-facing member communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping duties: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics + governance/usability into one bullet focused on improving cross-channel operations.
- Make technical work outcome-led: “Built Drupal microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits that accelerated campaign launches and improved content reuse.”
- Recast AI/search bullet to emphasize leadership and value: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating governance, analytics, and enterprise web modernization language already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role unless this entry shows new scope or results.
- Specific projects like the microsite and AI search are already named in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/organizational scope, and distinguish strategic leadership here from execution-heavy accomplishments covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: team size, budget size, growth in engagement, reporting efficiency, production savings, or turnaround improvements from the in-house studio and analytics stack.
- Tighten channel bullet: combine email/social reach with strategic purpose, e.g., “Oversaw core outreach channels reaching tens of thousands of county officials and supporting advocacy, member engagement, and event promotion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video-program growth overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this item focused on building the studio/capability, not recurring production.
- Governance/editorial workflow language overlaps with the current consultant role; stress enterprise leadership and modernization here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and relevant scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with sharper outcomes and less generic “helped” language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Ran NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Replace weak verbs: change “helping scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” to “scaled,” “standardized,” “streamlined,” or “established.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter open/click performance, audience growth, video cadence/views, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Possible version: “Managed NACo’s daily digital communications operations across web, email, social and video; oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials; launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update; and standardized editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video” and “weekly updates” overlap with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel.
- “Publishing workflows” and cross-team coordination also overlap with the 2022–2024 role; avoid sounding like the same job at a smaller title.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications
- Editorial governance and cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered advocacy and member communications
- Consider dropping “Audience-focused content planning,” which reads junior compared with the rest of the CV.
- If space allows, add one scale cue to increase credibility, e.g. “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header summary and multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress only if it is important for target roles; recent experience is overwhelmingly Drupal-led.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and discovery” for stronger, clearer business value.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority item to improve scanability and avoid a crowded list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level and reserve detailed tools there.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten vague items: change “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboarding and decision support”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX and content performance analysis” if those are true strengths
- Consider this full rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo experience bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, distinctive production capabilities rather than generic video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrasing with a sharper, more senior framing: “Broadcast-quality multimedia production” instead of “Video production and editing.”
- Group related items and reduce listiness, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production, editing, and studio operations
- Livestream and hybrid/virtual event production
- PTZ camera systems and multi-camera workflows
- If accurate, add scope/level signals tied to recent work: “in-house studio buildout,” “recurring advocacy programming,” or “executive/event livestream delivery.”
- Keep wording consistent with the rest of the CV’s leadership tone; this section should signal capability, not repeat tasks.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in the Director/Associate roles, so this skills item should stay concise and differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add context on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, high-value platforms first: **Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • SharePoint (intranet/content management) • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to sharpen scope: **CMS & Web Platforms**
- Keep it concise; avoid listing platforms that are not meaningfully supported elsewhere unless you can show usage level.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more tool-focused and the other more capability-focused.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overexplaining it here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broader platform categories.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and seniority: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome signals tied to recent work, e.g. “for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider trimming older/less differentiating items if space is tight; keep the tools most connected to current consulting and director-level work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep detail here and shorten the Topline version
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics/tooling sections; place it here only if emphasizing implementation rather than reporting

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and category-led so it supports recent leadership work rather than repeating broad PM tools.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and trim lower-value tools: “Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Work management & collaboration: Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Remove Basecamp and Trello unless they were materially used in recent roles; older/general tools dilute seniority.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”
- If space allows, add light context in the heading or nearby summary, e.g., “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, and reporting workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Jira/Asana/Slack are common collaboration tools; listing too many can make the section feel less strategic.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal platform administration and campaign execution without repeating broader “multi-channel communications” claims already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and clarify platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add light functional context instead of just tools: **Email campaign platforms, newsletter operations, audience journeys, and member communications**
- Best rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email newsletters, campaign journeys, audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in Work Experience.
- Don’t repeat generic phrases like “multi-channel communications” or “digital strategy,” which are already covered in Core Competencies and recent roles.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it tighter and more capability-led, with only the most relevant tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace vague terms like “Dashboarding” with stronger capability language such as “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- Consider swapping “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” only if you’ve directly run tests; otherwise keep “A/B testing” only where supported by experience.
- Order by strategic value and recency: lead with GA4, BigQuery, reporting tools, then optimization methods.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Differentiate this section as tool-focused and keep broader capabilities in Topline Skills.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating extra descriptors here unless they add specificity.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team-building impact: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping establish workflows for web, email, social and multimedia production.”
- Add concrete execution/results: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand member-facing communications.” Add counts if possible (events streamed, videos produced, audience growth, email volume).
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- Keep this entry shorter than 2018–2024 roles so the more senior positions carry more weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/production phase.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame here as helping establish initial processes, not leading them.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities at NACo.”
- Make the second sentence more outcome-oriented: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational initiatives, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outputs: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of research/projects supported.
- Keep this item concise; let later roles carry broader digital leadership, governance, and multimedia scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media roles; avoid broad multimedia claims here.
- Podcast/audio work is the best distinctive detail, since video/livestream leadership is already covered more strongly in later entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only and avoid repeating production capabilities already demonstrated in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to focus on software: “Creative Software” or “Multimedia Tools.”
- Tighten to tool names first; move workflow phrases out unless tied to a platform.
- Suggested rewrite: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want one capability phrase, make it more specific and current: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio systems”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations,” “Hybrid and virtual event production”) and recent NACo experience.
- “Podcast production” is already supported in older work experience; keep it only if podcasting is a target-role priority.
